testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A vehicle with air brakes traveling at 55 mph in good conditions needs about ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes time to see and react to a hazard, brake system delay, and actual braking. An air brake-equipped vehicle at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely in ideal conditions.

questions.question: What should you do if the brake pedal does not build up pressure?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.explanation: If you lose brake pressure, shift to a lower gear. This will help slow down your vehicle.

questions.question: In a convex mirror, objects look ____ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: A convex mirror makes objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Federal and state laws require:

options.text: Drivers to check their vehicles regularly.
Drivers to check their vehicles only if they think something is wrong.
Drivers to check their vehicles only when traveling out of state.
Drivers to check their vehicles only when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers to check their vehicles regularly.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must inspect their vehicles before every trip by law. Regular checks help you find problems before they become dangerous or costly.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the driver does not see you.
Wait for the other driver to signal it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians do not see you. This is an important safety precaution.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be checked:

options.text: To make sure they are clear.
To make sure they connect to the battery.
For the right amount of brake fluid.

questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, look at the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Check the hoses carefully for any leaks.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park in a busy area near trees.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop right away. Park in an open space away from trees and other vehicles that could catch fire. Do not go to a gas station.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Points are taken away for each pull-up.
You are allowed three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up only counts if you get out of the vehicle.
Only too many pull-ups count as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only too many pull-ups count as errors.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, one pull-up is allowed without penalty. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: While driving, you should stop and rest ____ to prevent tiredness.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, take a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles.

questions.question: Bent lock rings:
questions.explanation: Bent, cracked, or mismatched lock rings are dangerous and should not be used.

questions.question: What should you do during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Do it in the same order every time.
Only do it when the weather is sunny.
Skip it if the vehicle seems to be working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do it in the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Complete your pre-trip inspection the same way before each drive. This helps you remember all the steps and prevents you from forgetting to check something.

questions.question: What does intrastate driving mean?

options.text: Driving from one state to another

questions.explanation: Intrastate driving means you drive a commercial vehicle only within one state, and your cargo does not start or end outside that state.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: How should you use mirrors while driving?

options.text: Stare in them for long periods.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Staring at mirrors for too long is dangerous because you will travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.

questions.question: Where must hazard placards be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: On the front, back, and both sides

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, back, and both sides
questions.explanation: When carrying hazardous materials, you must place the same placard on the front, back, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When must you sign a written vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Only if defects were found and fixed or determined to not need fixing
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000
Only if a police officer asks you to

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and fixed or determined to not need fixing
questions.explanation: Sign the inspection report only if defects were noted and certified to have been repaired or determined not to need repair.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air becomes old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: How should you press the brake pedal when stopping?

options.text: Press it down gradually and smoothly
Press it repeatedly, but not continuously
Use the same amount of force every time

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down gradually and smoothly
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually each time you slow down or stop. The amount of brake pressure needed depends on your vehicle's speed and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: Why must drivers inspect their vehicles?

options.text: It is required by federal and state law

questions.correctAnswerText: It is required by federal and state law
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving to ensure they are safe to operate.

questions.question: If you must drive very slowly, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers, if local law allows.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used at every wheel. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: What should you do if you find something unsafe during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Continue driving and schedule a mechanic visit after the trip
Let a more experienced driver use the vehicle
Have the problem fixed right away
Avoid using only the unsafe items and continue driving normally

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the problem fixed right away
questions.explanation: If a pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, you must fix it immediately. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: How should you stop your vehicle in an emergency?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop
Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle going straight
Brake in a way that turns your vehicle
Expect your vehicle to slow down much faster than normal

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle going straight
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. It is important to brake in a way that keeps your vehicle traveling straight while still allowing you to turn if needed.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pushing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
The distance from where the brake pedal rests to the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle
How worn out the brakes are

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pushing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
questions.explanation: Air brakes have a delay because air takes time to travel through the air lines. Brake lag is usually at least half a second after you press the pedal. Hydraulic brakes work instantly when you press the pedal.

questions.question: Which item is NOT acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and a working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What do you need to do to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Have no moving violations on your record
Promise to be a good driver

questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check, which includes being fingerprinted.

questions.question: What does a maximum safe speed sign mean?

options.text: It suggests a speed, but you can drive faster
It only applies to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds
You must follow it and never drive faster than the posted speed

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow it and never drive faster than the posted speed
questions.explanation: You must never go faster than the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: What must an air tank in an air-brake vehicle have?
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have one-way check valves between the air compressor and the first reservoir. This stops air from leaking out if there is a problem.

questions.question: What gets removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These can build up and damage the brakes.

questions.question: What air pressure must build up in both systems before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build pressure of at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: After you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once you start moving.

questions.explanation: When the engine starts, all warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately. This includes the charging circuit light, oil light, coolant light, and ABS light.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, it:

options.text: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Pushes the brake lining against the wheel.
Releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, it pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Drive with one foot on the gas and one foot on the brake.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, you must bring the vehicle to a safe stop as soon as possible while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the back of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave open space on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side.
questions.explanation: When turning right, keep the back of your vehicle close to the curb. Do not leave space on your right side. This space might tell other drivers you are turning left, and they may try to pass you on the right.

questions.question: If you need to drive in reverse, it is helpful to:

options.text: Exit the vehicle and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Stick your head out the window and look back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the vehicle and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk around your vehicle to look for hazards. Use both mirrors while backing and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: When an oncoming vehicle has bright headlights at night, you can avoid being blinded by:

options.text: Looking to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looking to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights at night, look to the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, your vehicle's speed will likely:

options.text: Match the speed of other traffic.

questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle speed up when going downhill. Before going downhill, choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: When visibility is poor, such as at dawn or dusk, what is the best way to make your vehicle visible?
questions.explanation: In poor visibility (dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights. Do not use high beams when driving near other vehicles.

questions.question: According to the National Sleep Foundation, about ____ of people have driven while sleepy.
questions.explanation: The National Sleep Foundation found that 60 percent of Americans have driven while sleepy. About 36 percent admit to falling asleep while driving.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be:

options.text: Asked to explain what you know about the inspection process.
Watching someone else inspect your vehicle.
Watching a video about vehicle inspection.
Changing all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Asked to explain what you know about the inspection process.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You will need to explain what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: When should you NOT use the parking brake?

options.text: When your vehicle is stopped on a level surface.
When your vehicle is stopped on a slight incline.
When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
When your vehicle's other braking systems are working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from driving downhill or if they are wet and it is freezing. Hot brakes can be damaged by the parking brake. Wet brakes in freezing weather can ice up and lock your wheels.

questions.question: How can you reduce braking when driving downhill?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going down a hill. This helps your vehicle maintain a safe speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle must not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer after the vehicle is back on course.

questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brake pedal so the wheels can roll again. Steer quickly in the direction you want to go, then countersteer to prevent the vehicle from skidding the other way. Do not accelerate.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Make sure the truck is not overloaded.
Make sure the cargo is balanced.
Make sure the cargo is secured properly.
Place breakable items under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place breakable items under heavier items.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is properly secured, balanced, and within weight limits. Do not put breakable items under heavy items.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and disengage the parking brake.
Quickly press and release the brake pedal several times.
Uncouple and recouple all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly press and release the brake pedal several times.
questions.explanation: After the air system has charged, test the low pressure warning signal by quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air from the system. The warning light should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to shift gears. It takes practice to do this correctly.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: When inspecting a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This should take about 45 seconds.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern if no passengers are getting off.
Should not be on the roadway.
Is always a concern, whether you can see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether you can see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind it. The bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front area for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.
